version: v3 (2026-10-25), direct end-effector wall contact; supersedes v2 (33 cm probe, unconnected mount)
status: candidate: centred supplied mount (continuous, no added mass), beta 20 deg, pad 12 mm; from results/am3_design/ (scan.json, patch_clearance.txt)

pad.note: rubber contact button between the finger tips, centred on the supplied ee site, 12 mm radius (protrudes 12 mm beyond the finger faces; it overlaps the finger inner faces by 2 mm, same body); mass is part of the supplied 0.10 kg hand

yaw_housing.note: ASSUMPTION: XM430-class servo mass; the supplied drone inertial (1.05 kg) is taken to include it (only matters if the mount is moved)

bracket.note: carbon plate under the airframe core, only present when mount_x_m > 0

servo.source: RobotShop listing and ROBOTIS brochure (3.0 N m, 77 rpm, 82 g @12 V); continuous 1/3 stall is an ASSUMPTION

propulsion.source: SIMULATION ASSUMPTION (unchanged from v2): 7-inch-class prop, D = 0.178 m, static Ct ~ 0.11 -> 10 N at ~16 krpm (1700 rad/s); no published table for the supplied vehicle. kf = f_max / omega_max^2. Sensitivity +-20 % is part of the mismatch suite.

contact.note: pad compression stands in for the elastic rubber pad: 600 N/m, 6 mm of compression (50 % of the 12 mm pad radius) gives 3.6 N, so F_max = 4 N. mu = 0.15 (PTFE-capped pad): friction force x pad lever (0.28 m) is a yaw moment the rotors can only cancel through the 0.016 m drag arm, see Findings/Codebase/aerial_manipulator_design_v3.md; mu = 0.3 is a robustness case.

task.note: patch limited by yaw authority (normal force x lateral offset) and by finger/wall clearance, results/am3_design/
